excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) enables language models to improve text-to-image (T2I) generation by rewriting prompts for a frozen image generator. We propose SCOPE, an objective based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) that aligns update weighting with this structure. title: DeltaStreamer: Towards Human-Like Agentic Streaming Video Understanding
excerpt: We propose DeltaStreamer, a novel agentic framework for streaming video understanding inspired by how humans observe, remember, and investigate. Streaming video understanding requires a system to retain evidence before knowing which details future queries will need. Existing approaches often obscure event transitions and omit relevant details when compressing video history, and cannot recover missing visual evidence. DeltaStreamer addresses these limitations by combining change-aware memory with query-driven planning and targeted evidence gathering with replay. ai.summary: DeltaStreamer is an agentic framework for streaming video understanding that uses change‑aware memory to retain evidence for future queries, mimicking human observation patterns.
ai.why: Provides a foundation for building video‑analysis agents that can answer queries about past events without losing detail.

title: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
excerpt: Spatial intelligence lets an agent perceive and act in the physical world, and many of its judgments must be made at interaction rates: which spatial relation holds, how far an object is, or where to place it. Vision-language models (VLMs) produce these answers by free-form text generation, paying for autoregressive decoding and answer parsing even though the output space is compact: one of a few options, a scalar, or a 2D point. In light of this, we introduce MJev-Spatial, a System 1 multimodal decision model that tackles all three types of spatial understanding tasks within a unified classification framework. ai.summary: The paper introduces MJev-Spatial, a System 1 multimodal model that uses native attention matching to answer spatial questions (relations, distances, positions) with compact outputs instead of autoregressive text generation.
ai.why: It offers faster, lower‑cost spatial reasoning useful for real‑time robotics or AR applications.

title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
excerpt: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. ai.summary: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed‑forward Gaussian splatting by separating geometry and attribute prediction and adding a frozen geometry branch, boosting novel‑view rendering quality from arbitrary viewpoints.
ai.why: Offers a more robust open‑source method for real‑time 3D reconstruction that developers can integrate into graphics pipelines.

title: Orbia: Do Generated Videos Form a Consistent 3D World?
excerpt: Video generators serve as interactive worlds for exploration and simulation, yet realistic and visually appealing frames do not necessarily depict a consistent 3D world. We introduce Orbia, the first benchmark dedicated to a systematic and comprehensive evaluation of 3D consistency in interactive world models. Through controlled exploration and revisit, we organize the evaluation into three dimensions: input preservation, generated-content persistence, and 3D self-consistency. ai.summary: Orbia introduces a benchmark that evaluates video generators for consistent 3D world modeling, measuring geometry and memory across interactive frames.

title: RoTA-Bench: Evaluating 3D Spatial Reasoning through Interactive Projection Alignment
excerpt: Can vision-language models turn 2D observations into 3D understanding that supports precise action? Given a target silhouette, a model observes a rotated object and chooses successive rotations to recover the target projection within a limited action budget. excerpt: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer semantic knowledge acquired through vision-language pretraining to robot control, achieving strong performance across various benchmarks. excerpt: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) represent model activations with sparse, linearly decoded features, but the downstream effects of those features need not compose additively. We introduce SAE Additivity Residuals (SAR), which measure the behavioral variation left unexplained above a chosen interaction order. excerpt: Harness self-evolution revises an agent's software scaffolding, including prompts, memory, workflows, and executable components, while keeping model weights fixed. excerpt: Computer use has reached a turning point: the focus is expanding from GUI-only interaction to systems that complete tasks on users' computers through visual and programmatic interfaces. excerpt: Audio source separation models must preserve fine spectral structure while keeping the cost of the separator tractable. title: Each Reward to Its Relevant Tokens: Reward-Specific Token-Level Credit Assignment for Multi-Reward RL
excerpt: Language models are increasingly trained against several verifiable rewards at once, such as the correctness and the format of a tool call, or the individual constraints of a complex instruction. We propose MRTPO, which assigns the advantage of each reward to the tokens relevant to it, using the information its verifier checks, without auxiliary models or token-level annotations. title: Mosaic: Multi-Session Agentic Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Most existing agentic reinforcement learning methods assume single-session trajectories, where interaction proceeds within one continuously accumulated context. title: Speculative Forcing for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
excerpt: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early.
